scenarios.location: Medical-surgical floor at a busy hour
scenarios.problem: Every device shares the 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz bands with older equipment and neighboring units, so capacity runs short when the floor is busiest.
scenarios.outcomeSupported: Moving capable devices to 6 GHz frees capacity in the older bands and gives imaging and video wider channels, free of older devices.

scenarios.problem: A nurse's badge call stutters when a large imaging upload fills the one band the badge is connected to.
scenarios.outcomeSupported: With multi-link operation, the call's packets can use a less busy band, supporting steadier calls on the move.

scenarios.problem: Devices share a long-lived WPA2 password that a recorded sign-in could crack offline, and staff devices could be fooled by a fake access point.
scenarios.outcomeSupported: WPA3 makes offline guessing ineffective on shared-password networks and makes staff devices check they are on the real network, supporting the organization’s wider security program.

scenarios.location: Inpatient unit across a long shift
scenarios.problem: Small battery-powered devices keep their radios listening and need recharging or swapping before the shift ends.
scenarios.outcomeSupported: Target Wake Time lets devices sleep between agreed wake-ups, and optional Restricted TWT can protect time for voice and telemetry on devices that support it, so batteries can last longer and timing can be more predictable.

scenarios.location: Imaging and procedure rooms during a busy shift
scenarios.problem: Large imaging studies and video consults hold the channel for a long time, so other devices on the same channel wait behind them.
scenarios.outcomeSupported: On devices that support it, Wi-Fi 7’s wider channels and denser signals finish transfers sooner and give the air back to everyone else; real speeds depend on the device and its distance.
